meaning: to travel; to take a trip

senses.en: to travel, take a trip (去 + place + 旅行)
a trip, a journey (这次旅行 'this trip')

measure.note: 一次旅行 'a trip'; 趟 is also used (这趟旅行)

examples.en: We're traveling to China next year.
examples.analysis: 去中国旅行 is two verbs in a row: 去 'go (to China)' and 旅行 'travel', which gives the purpose. The destination goes with 去 in front of it: 去 + 中国 + 旅行, 'go to China to travel'. 旅行 normally takes no place object, so this is the usual pattern. 明年 'next year' sits before the verbs, as time words do.

examples.zh: 你平时喜欢去哪儿旅行？
examples.en: Where do you usually like to travel?
examples.analysis: 去哪儿旅行 'go where to travel' is the thing you like, so the whole chunk follows 喜欢. The question word 哪儿 stays in the place slot where the answer would go (去北京旅行); the word order does not change for the question.

examples.zh: 我不想去旅行，想在家休息。
examples.en: I don't feel like traveling; I want to rest at home.
examples.analysis: 不想去旅行 'don't want to go traveling': 不 negates 想, and 去旅行 is the plan being turned down. The second clause drops the subject 我 because it is the same person, and 在家休息 'rest at home' is offered instead.

collocations.en: to go to … on a trip

related.en: to tour, travel for sightseeing; very common for holiday trips

senses.en: hotel (the usual sense in mainland China today)
(older or literary use) a tavern, a wine shop

measure.note: 一家酒店; 个 is also heard

examples.zh: 我们的酒店离机场很近。
examples.en: Our hotel is close to the airport.
examples.analysis: 我们的酒店 'our hotel' is the subject. A 离 B 近 = 'A is close to B': 离 marks the place you measure from, and the adjective 近 'near' is the predicate, with no 是 in between.

examples.en: How's the hotel you're staying at?
examples.analysis: 你们住的 'that you are staying in' describes 酒店: the describer comes first, then 的, then the noun. 怎么样 at the end asks for an opinion: 'how is it?'. 住 is the verb for staying at a hotel.

examples.en: This hotel isn't too expensive.
examples.analysis: 家 is the measure word for businesses such as hotels, shops and restaurants: 这 + 家 + 酒店 'this hotel'. 不太贵 'not too expensive' is milder than 不贵 'not expensive'.

related.en: restaurant; also in some hotel names (北京饭店)

meaning: at any time; at any moment

senses.en: (at) any time, whenever you like: 随时问我 'ask me anytime'
at any moment, could happen any minute (随时会…)

examples.en: If you have any questions, ask me anytime.
examples.analysis: 随时 sits before the verb 问 'ask', like other adverbs. 有问题 'have a question' sets the condition with no word for 'if'; putting it first is enough to make it the condition.

examples.en: Can I come and see you anytime?
examples.analysis: 随时 comes after 可以 'may' and before the verb phrase 来找你 'come and find you'. The speaker asks for permission that holds at any time; 吗 turns the statement into a yes-no question.

examples.en: He could get here any minute, so don't leave yet.
examples.analysis: With 会 'will, is likely to', 随时 means 'at any moment': 随时会到 'could arrive any minute'. The second clause, 先别走 'don't leave yet', combines 先 'for now' with 别 'don't'.

collocations.en: to get in touch anytime (有事随时联系 'contact me anytime if anything comes up')

related.en: when; 什么时候都可以 'any time works'

meaning: to learn by heart; to recite from memory

senses.en: to memorize, learn by heart (背生词 'memorize new words')
to recite from memory, say without looking

examples.en: I memorized ten new words today.
examples.analysis: 背 is the verb 'memorize', and 了 marks the job as done. 十个生词 'ten new words' is the object, with number + 个 before the noun. 背生词 is a normal way to say 'learn vocabulary by heart' (背单词 is just as common).

examples.en: Can you recite it for me?
examples.analysis: Here 背 means 'recite from memory'. 背给我听 is literally 'recite for me to hear': 给我 names the listener and 听 'listen' completes the picture. 'It' is left out because both people know what is meant.

examples.en: Stop memorizing and take a break.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb + 了 here asks someone to stop what they are doing: 别背了 'stop memorizing'. Without 了, 别背 would be 'don't memorize (it)'. The same pattern can also call off a plan, as in 别去了 'don't go after all'. 先休息吧 'rest first' suggests what to do instead.

collocations.en: to learn a text by heart

related.en: to carry on one's back (背包 'backpack'): a different word, first tone

senses.en: degree of temperature or angle: 三十度 '30 degrees'
kilowatt-hour on an electricity bill (一度电)
degree, extent (in words like 温度 'temperature')

examples.en: It's 35 degrees today. It's too hot.
examples.analysis: 度 comes straight after the number, with no 个: 三十五度 '35 degrees'. Temperatures in China are given in Celsius. The number phrase is the predicate on its own, with no verb: 今天三十五度 'today (is) 35 degrees'.

examples.zh: 他三十九度了，快带他去医院吧。
examples.en: His temperature's up to 39°C (102°F) now. Hurry and take him to the hospital.
examples.analysis: Said of a person, 三十九度 means body temperature, so this is a high fever. 了 marks the new situation: it has gone up to 39. 快 + verb urges speed: 快带他去 'hurry and take him'.

examples.en: What's the temperature tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 多少 'how many' takes the place of the number, right before 度: 多少度 'how many degrees?'. This is a common way to ask about the forecast (几度 works too), and no verb is needed.

meaning: measure word for class periods; festival

senses.en: for class periods and lessons: 三节课 'three classes'
for sections of something long, such as train carriages
festival, holiday (in 节日, 春节)

examples.en: I have three classes today.
examples.analysis: 节 counts class periods: 三 + 节 + 课 'three classes'. It is the usual measure word for lessons at school or university. 有 'have' + the count states the day's timetable.

examples.en: What time is the next class?
examples.analysis: 下 + 节 + 课 = 'the next class', with no 一 needed; 上节课 is 'the last class'. 几点 'what time' asks for a clock time, and 是 is left out, as it often is before times.

examples.en: I didn't go to the last class.
examples.analysis: 上节课 'the last class' is moved to the front as the topic. 没 + verb negates a past event: 没去 'didn't go'. The same 上/下 + measure word pattern gives 上次 'last time' and 下次 'next time'.

meaning: row, line; measure word for things in a row

senses.en: row (of seats or people): 第一排 'the front row'
for things in a row: 一排椅子 'a row of chairs'

examples.en: Let's sit in the front row.
examples.analysis: 第一排 'the first row' is the front row in a cinema, hall or classroom; 第 turns the number into 'first'. It goes right after 坐 'sit' as the place, and 吧 makes the sentence a suggestion.

examples.en: Which row is your seat in?
examples.analysis: 第几排 'which row?' puts the question word 几 in the number slot of 第_排. 在 + place says where the seat is, and the answer copies the frame: 在第五排 'in row five'.

examples.en: There's nobody in that back row.
examples.analysis: Here 排 is the measure word after 那 'that': 那排 'that row'. 后边 'at the back' in front of it says which row. 没有人 'there is nobody' is the plain way to say the row is empty.

collocations.en: back row; back seat of a car

related.en: to arrange, line up (排队 'stand in line'): a different sense, not covered in this entry

senses.en: many, a lot of (before a noun: 许多人 'many people')
a lot, much (after a verb or adjective: 好了许多 'much better')

examples.en: He has a lot of Chinese friends.
examples.analysis: 许多 goes straight before the noun phrase, with no measure word: 许多 + 中国朋友. It means the same as 很多 here; 很多 is more common in everyday talk, and 许多 sounds a little more formal.

examples.zh: 这件事许多人都不知道。
examples.en: A lot of people don't know about this.
examples.analysis: 这件事 'this matter' is moved to the front as the topic. 许多人 'many people' is the subject, and 都 sums them up before the negative 不知道 'don't know'. The claim is about many people, not everyone.

examples.en: I have so much I want to tell you.
examples.analysis: 许多话 'many words' is what I have; 想跟你说 'want to say to you' follows and says what they are for. 跟你 marks the listener, so 跟你说 is 'say to you'.

related.en: quite a few, quite a lot
many, much; 很多 is the everyday 'a lot of'

senses.en: a bottle of: 一瓶水 'a bottle of water'
bottle (as a thing, speech usually says 瓶子)

measure.note: 一个瓶子 'a bottle' (the noun usually takes 子)

examples.en: Two more bottles of water, please.
examples.analysis: 瓶 is the measure word: 两 + 瓶 + 水. Before a measure word, 'two' on its own is normally 两, not 二. 来 is the everyday ordering verb, roughly 'we'll have / bring us', and 再 'again' makes it 'two more'.

examples.zh: 我买了一瓶酒，晚上一起喝吧。
examples.en: I bought a bottle of wine. Let's drink it together tonight.
examples.analysis: 一瓶酒 'a bottle of alcohol' (English would usually say 'wine' or 'liquor' here): number + 瓶 + the drink. 酒 covers any alcoholic drink, from beer to baijiu. In the second clause the object of 喝 is dropped because the bottle was just mentioned.

examples.en: Is this milk still OK to drink?
examples.analysis: 这 + 瓶 + 牛奶 'this bottle of milk': after 这 or 那, the number 一 is usually dropped. 还能喝吗 'can it still be drunk?' asks whether it has gone off.

related.en: a cup or glass of (一杯水)

senses.en: smooth, without a hitch (a trip, work, a plan)
in good wishes: 一路顺利 'have a good trip', 工作顺利 'hope work goes well'

examples.en: Did you have a smooth trip?
examples.analysis: A standard question for someone who has just arrived. 路上 'on the way' is the topic and 顺利 is the predicate: 'was it smooth?'. Like other adjectives, 顺利 works as the predicate without 是.

examples.en: Today's meeting went smoothly.
examples.analysis: 开会 'hold a meeting' is split: the object 会 moves to the front as the topic, and 开 + 得 + 很顺利 says how it went. Verb + 得 + adjective is the usual way to rate how something was done.

examples.en: Work hasn't been going very well lately.
examples.analysis: 不太顺利 'not very smooth' is a gentle way to admit that things are going badly. 最近 'lately' sets the time, and 工作 'work' is the topic.

collocations.en: all the best; hope everything goes well

senses.en: to change (a time, a plan, a habit): 改时间 'reschedule'
to correct, fix a mistake (改错 'correct errors')

examples.en: Could I change the time?
examples.analysis: 改 + 个 + 时间: 个 is a short 一个, so this is 'change to a (different) time', i.e. reschedule. 能…吗 asks whether it is possible. 改时间 is the everyday way to move a meeting or appointment.

examples.en: There's a mistake here. Let me fix it.
examples.analysis: 写错了 'written wrong' points out the mistake, so 改 here means 'correct'. 我来 + verb volunteers: 'let me do it'. The object is dropped because 'it' is clear from the first clause.

examples.en: These habits are hard to change.
examples.analysis: 难 + verb = 'hard to do': 难改 'hard to change'. The thing being changed, 这些习惯 'these habits', comes first as the topic, and 很难改 is the comment about it.

related.en: to change, become different (on its own)

meaning: quite a lot; quite a few

senses.en: quite a lot of, quite a few (before a noun: 不少人)
quite a bit (after a verb: 变了不少 'changed quite a bit')

examples.en: Quite a lot of people came today.
examples.analysis: 不少人 'quite a few people' comes after the verb 来了. With verbs of arriving, Chinese often puts new, unspecified people after the verb. 不少 goes straight before the noun with no measure word.

examples.en: Beijing has changed quite a bit in the last few years.
examples.analysis: After verb + 了, 不少 tells how much: 变了不少 'changed quite a bit'. 这几年 'these few years' sets the time span at the start, and 北京 is the subject.

examples.en: You must have spent quite a bit of money, right?
examples.analysis: 不少钱 'quite a bit of money' is the object of 花 'spend'. 吧 at the end marks a guess the speaker expects you to confirm, which is softer than a plain 吗 question.

meaning: a good thing; good news; a good deed

senses.en: a good thing, good news: 是好事 'it's a good thing'
a good deed (做好事 'do a good deed')
(sarcastic) 看你干的好事！ 'Look what you've done!'

examples.zh: 有什么好事啊？看你这么高兴。
examples.en: What's the good news? You look so happy.
examples.analysis: 有什么好事啊 'what good thing has happened?' asks for the news, and 啊 makes the question sound friendly. 看你这么高兴 'looking at how happy you are' gives the reason for asking: 看 here means 'judging by'. 这么 + adjective = 'so…'.

examples.en: Exercising more is a good thing.
examples.analysis: The phrase 多运动 'exercising more' is the subject, and 是好事 'is a good thing' is the verdict. 多 before a verb means 'do more of it'.

examples.en: This isn't a good thing at all.
examples.analysis: 不是什么 + noun = 'not any kind of…', a stronger denial than plain 不是好事. 什么 does not ask a question here; it widens the 'no'.

senses.en: guest, visitor (at someone's home)
customer, client (in a shop, hotel or restaurant)

measure.note: 一位客人 (polite); 个 in casual speech

examples.en: We're having guests over tonight.
examples.analysis: 家里有客人 'there are guests at home': 有 means 'there is/are', with the place 家里 before it. The English 'we' is not in the Chinese; it is understood from 家里 'at (our) home'.

examples.en: Have the guests arrived?
examples.analysis: 客人 is the subject. Nouns usually carry no plural marking, so it can be 'the guest' or 'the guests'. 到了 'have arrived' plus 吗 asks whether it has happened.

examples.en: There aren't many customers in the shop today.
examples.analysis: In a shop, 客人 means 'customers'. 店里 'in the shop' and 今天 'today' set the scene, and 客人不多 'customers are not many' is the comment.

collocations.en: to look after guests, entertain visitors

senses.en: to exercise, work out
sport, exercise (运动 as a thing you do)
movement, campaign (political or social)

measure.note: 一项运动 'a sport'; 种 for 'a kind of'; 场 for a campaign (一场运动)

examples.en: Do you usually exercise?
examples.analysis: 运动 is a verb here, 'to exercise', and it needs no object. 平时 'usually, normally' asks about habits, not about today. 吗 makes it a yes-no question.

examples.zh: 我最喜欢的运动是打篮球。
examples.en: My favorite sport is basketball.
examples.analysis: Here 运动 is a noun, 'sport', described by 我最喜欢的 'that I like most'. The sport itself is said as an action, 打篮球 'play basketball', which English shortens to 'basketball'.

examples.en: Don't exercise right after a meal.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb phrase advises against something: 别马上运动 'don't exercise right away'. The warning is about timing, not about exercise itself, because 马上 'right away' sits inside what 别 negates. 吃饭以后 'after eating' sets the time first, as time phrases usually do.

senses.en: to climb (stairs, a mountain): 爬山 'go hiking'
to crawl (babies, insects)

examples.en: Let's go hiking this weekend!
examples.analysis: 爬山 'climb a mountain' is the everyday word for a hiking trip, even up a modest hill. 去 + 爬山 = 'go hiking', 一起 'together' comes before it, and 吧 turns the whole thing into a suggestion.

examples.en: The baby can crawl now.
examples.analysis: Here 爬 means 'crawl'. 会 + verb + 了 announces a newly learned skill: 'can do it now', with the sense that the child could not before. 孩子 'child' covers babies too.

examples.zh: 我爬不动了，休息一会儿吧。
examples.en: I can't climb any farther. Let's rest for a bit.
examples.analysis: 爬不动 = 'too tired to climb (any more)': verb + 不动 says the action can't go on for lack of strength (with heavy things, as in 搬不动, it means 'too heavy to move'). 了 marks the change: I could before, I can't now. 休息一会儿 'rest a while' with 吧 suggests a break.

collocations.en: to go hiking, climb a mountain

senses.en: romantic love (between partners), not love for family or friends

measure.note: 一段爱情 'a romance, a love affair'; 一份爱情 in songs and writing; rarely counted in casual speech

examples.en: Do you believe in love?
examples.analysis: 爱情 is the object of 相信 'believe (in)'; English needs 'in', Chinese does not. 爱情 is the noun for romantic love, while the verb 'to love' is 爱.

examples.en: I don't like watching romance movies.
examples.analysis: 爱情 sits directly before 电影 with no 的: 爱情电影 'romance films'. There are two 爱s here: 不爱看 'don't like to watch' uses the verb 爱, and 爱情 names the genre.

examples.zh: 他们的爱情故事很有意思。
examples.en: Their love story is really interesting.
examples.analysis: 爱情故事 'love story' is noun + noun. 他们的 'their' sits in front, and 很有意思 'very interesting' is the comment. 有意思 is the everyday word for 'interesting'.

senses.en: very, extremely (a bit more formal than 很 or 非常)
with 不: 不十分 / 不是十分 'not entirely, not fully'

examples.en: Thank you so much for your help.
examples.analysis: 十分 strengthens the verb 感谢 'thank'. 十分感谢 is a set polite formula in emails, speeches and thank-you notes; between friends, 太谢谢你了 is more relaxed. 你的帮助 'your help' is the object.

examples.en: Dr. Wang is extremely conscientious.
examples.analysis: 十分 + adjective works like 很 or 非常: 十分认真 'very conscientious'. It sounds slightly formal and written; in casual talk people would usually say 很认真. 王医生 'Doctor Wang' is surname + title.

examples.en: I'm not entirely sure either.
examples.analysis: 不是十分 + adjective = 'not entirely…': 不是十分清楚 'not completely clear (to me)'. It softens 'I don't know' into 'I'm not quite sure'. 也 'also' links it to someone else's uncertainty.

meaning: to exceed, be more than; to overtake

senses.en: to be more than, exceed (a number or a limit)
to overtake, get ahead of (a car, a person, a rival)

examples.zh: 他一天工作超过十个小时。
examples.en: He works more than ten hours a day.
examples.analysis: 超过 + amount = 'more than': 超过十个小时 'over ten hours'. 一天 'a day, per day' comes before the verb as the time frame. 小时 takes 个 as its measure word: 十个小时.

examples.en: Will it come to more than a hundred kuai in total?
examples.analysis: 超过一百块 'more than 100 kuai' is the amount being asked about. 会 'will' makes it a guess about the bill, and 一共 'altogether' says we mean the total. 块 is the spoken word for yuan.

examples.zh: 你的包超过二十公斤了。
examples.en: Your bag is over twenty kilos.
examples.analysis: 超过 + limit + 了 says a limit has now been passed: the bag is over 20 kg. 公斤 is 'kilogram'; at the market people also weigh in 斤, half a kilo.

related.en: and above; includes the number itself (二十公斤以上 = 20 kg or more), unlike 超过

meaning: to recall, remember; to be reminded of

senses.en: to remember, recall (something you had forgotten)
to be reminded of, think of (想起小时候)

examples.en: I've suddenly remembered something.
examples.analysis: 想起 + object = 'recall something': 想起一件事. 忽然 'suddenly' shows it has just popped into the speaker's head. 一件事 'one matter' uses 件, the measure word for matters and affairs.

examples.en: Have you remembered his name?
examples.analysis: 想起 is getting back something you had forgotten, here 他的名字 'his name'. 了吗 asks whether that change has happened. In speech you will also hear the longer 想起来, as in 我想起来了！ 'Now I remember!'

examples.zh: 看到这些照片，我就想起小时候。
examples.en: When I see these photos, I think of my childhood.
examples.analysis: Here 想起 means 'be reminded of': seeing the photos brings childhood to mind. 看到…，就… links a trigger to what follows it straight away. 小时候 'when I was little' is the object.
